cases.text: RocketPhone.ai turns customer conversations into structured Salesforce data. It had that working for softphone calls, video meetings and in-person meetings. Mobile calls stayed dark, because a call placed from a rep’s handset never touches RocketPhone’s infrastructure. Every workaround fails for the same reason. Recording a native cellular call requires control of the voice path, and the voice path belongs to the mobile operator. RocketPhone had to become one. Rather than spend on telecom infrastructure, RocketPhone engage d Spenza as its MVNE . Spenza supplied carrier integration, eSIM provisioning, rating, billing, subscriber management and multi-tier reseller control, exposed through APIs. RocketPhone kept its engineering on conversation AI. The mechanism that makes it work: Spenza terminates calls on RocketPhone’s provisioned numbers to a SIP URI. The rep places an ordinary cellular call with no app and no data connection. The far leg lands inside RocketPhone’s platform, where it gets recorded, transcribed and written to Salesforce. Customer overview Field Details Company RocketPhone.ai Limited Headquarters London, United Kingdom Category Conversation intelligence for Salesforce Products RocketPhone Dialer, RocketVideo, RocketCell, and Vulnerability Detection Salesforce Status Certified ISV and listed on AppExchange RocketPhone sells one idea: Salesforce is only as useful as the data inside it, and the richest customer data is spoken out loud, then lost. Its platform captures conversations across channels and writes back transcripts, summaries, sentiment, topics, action items and deal signals as structured records. Its own customers describe the value in those terms. Sam Wilson, CTO at Bruntwood, says on RocketPhone’s site that buyers are “not replacing like for like on telephony”, and frames the purchase as access to business process data the company did not previously hold. The Business Problem: Mobile Calls Were a Hole in the Data Model RocketPhone’s thesis carries a dependency. Capture has to be total. Suppose a CRM logs most of a company’s customer conversations but misses the rest. That does not leave you with most of the insight. It leaves you with a forecast built on a biased sample, because the calls that go unlogged are not a random subset. They are the ones made by field staff, at customer sites, in car parks, on the move. Those are the conversations where deals turn. RocketPhone had solved capture for every channel it controlled. Softphone calls ran through its dialer. Video ran through RocketVideo. In-person meetings had a capture path. Mobile calls, placed from a handset over the cellular network, went nowhere near any of it. Three obvious fixes exist. Each one breaks. Ask reps to use a VoIP app. RocketPhone rejected this publicly, and its reasoning sits on rocketcell.ai: VoIP calls depend on data connectivity, which RocketPhone describes as unreliable in the field. A rep standing in a warehouse with one bar will not open an app to make a call. They will use the dialer on their phone. Any capture strategy that depends on changing that behaviour fails on contact with a sales team. Use the carrier’s call recording. This makes the operator a dependency for a core product feature. Recording quality, retention, API access and portability all sit with the MNO. Change operator and the integration is rebuilt. Serve a customer in a market where the operator offers nothing and the feature does not exist. Record on the handset. Mobile operating systems do not expose the native call audio path to third-party applications. The Constraint Every failed approach runs into the same fundamental limitation: recording a native cellular call requires control of the voice path . That voice path is controlled by the mobile network operator , not by the application running on the device. For RocketPhone , the objective was not to operate a mobile network. The goal was to capture native mobile calls directly in Salesforce . Achieving that required carrier-level control of the call flow, making operator capabilities the only practical path to delivering the desired experience. The Challenge RocketPhone wanted more than another mobile reseller program. The goal was to create a fully branded business mobile network that integrated directly with its UCaaS platform and Salesforce ecosystem while giving customers a seamless mobile experience. To make that possible, RocketPhone needed a platform that could: Launch branded SIM and eSIM services Support native voice, SMS, and data connectivity Integrate mobile services with its CRM and UCaaS platform Enable enterprise customers and channel partners through a multi-tier distribution model Automate provisioning, billing, subscription management, and ongoing operations Scale internationally without building telecom infrastructure from scratch Managing multiple carrier relationships, billing systems, provisioning platforms, and operational workflows internally would have significantly increased time to market. The Solution Spenza delivered a complete MVNE platform that enabled RocketPhone to launch its branded mobile service on top of a carrier-agnostic connectivity platform. The implementation included: White label RocketPhone portal for administrators, partners, and enterprise customers SIM and eSIM provisioning with API-based activation Native voice, SMS, and mobile data connectivity Multi-tier reseller and enterprise account management Automated billing and subscription management Marketplace access to mobile connectivity plans APIs for integrating mobile services directly into RocketPhone’s applications and CRM SIP routing support for enterprise voice workflows Mobile messaging APIs for inbound and outbound SMS Real-time dashboards for subscriptions, usage, revenue, and operational visibility These capabilities matched the deployment plan outlined during the project and allowed RocketPhone to launch a unified connectivity experience alongside its existing communications platform. Implementation The deployment followed a structured rollout that included platform configuration, carrier integration where required, onboarding, testing, and production readiness. Working closely with the RocketPhone team, Spenza configured the platform, integrated the required connectivity services, enabled enterprise onboarding workflows, and prepared the environment for launch. Results With Spenza, RocketPhone successfully launched a branded business mobile offering without building its own telecom stack. RocketPhone gained: A fully branded mobile connectivity platform Integrated eSIM, voice, SMS, and billing capabilities Enterprise-ready APIs Multi-tier reseller enablement Automated provisioning and subscription lifecycle management A scalable platform that supports future carrier expansion and additional markets The result is a unified platform where business mobile connectivity becomes a natural extension of RocketPhone’s AI-powered communications offering instead of a separate product. What Scaling Looks Like Next The platform’s modular design is what the proposal offers for growth: add operators, launch in new markets, extend with add-ons. In practice that means a few concrete moves for RocketPhone. More markets. RocketCell is UK-based today. Spenza’s marketplace model means a new market is a commercial decision about which operator plan to resell, not an engineering project. Reseller depth. RocketPhone’s Salesforce SI partners are a natural reseller tier. The platform already supports their markup, branding and billing. Self-serve. The proposal scopes eCommerce provisioning and Shopify. A customer buying a line without talking to sales changes the unit economics of the whole motion. API access downstream. The proposal includes offering API access to RocketPhone’s own customers, which turns the connectivity layer into something enterprises can automate against. Why It Matters Modern business communication extends beyond desk phones and video meetings. Mobile conversations are equally important, especially for sales teams, field employees, and customer-facing staff. By combining RocketPhone’s conversation intelligence platform with Spenza’s mobile connectivity infrastructure, enterprises can deliver business mobile services that integrate directly into their communication workflows while simplifying deployment, operations, and customer management. Instead of building telecom infrastructure, RocketPhone focused on delivering customer value while Spenza handled the complexity behind connectivity. About Spenza Spenza is a no-code MVNE platform that enables businesses to launch branded mobile services with APIs, eSIM provisioning, billing, compliance, reseller management, and access to a global connectivity marketplace. Companies use Spenza to launch and scale MVNOs, embedded connectivity offerings, and enterprise mobility solutions without the traditional complexity of telecom infrastructure. Key Takeaways Recording a native cellular call requires control of the voice path, and that means operating the network. There is no software shortcut. Termination to a SIP URI is the mechanism: the user’s leg stays cellular, the far leg lands in your platform. An MVNE removes the 12-to-15-month, multi-million-pound path to becoming an operator, which matters most when telecom is not what your customers buy. Multi-tier reseller structure lets a connectivity layer inherit an existing partner motion rather than force a new one. eSIM plus QR activation removes logistics from onboarding, which is where mobile rollouts usually stall. Conclusion RocketPhone’s journey demonstrates that delivering enterprise-grade mobile communications is not about building telecom infrastructure. It is about enabling seamless customer experiences while keeping engineering efforts focused on the core product. By partnering with Spenza, RocketPhone launched a fully branded business mobile network with native voice, eSIM, automated provisioning, billing, and Salesforce integration without taking on the complexity of operating a mobile network. With a scalable MVNE platform handling carrier integrations and connectivity operations, RocketPhone can continue expanding into new markets, support more enterprise customers and partners, and evolve its AI-powered communications platform with confidence. The result is a unified solution where mobile connectivity becomes a natural extension of conversation intelligence rather than a separate product. Daito helps businesses securely manage and share two-factor authentication across teams. Its web-based platform gives authorized users access to shared 2FA tokens while keeping administration, access controls, and auditability centralized. Daito is currently trusted by more than 250 businesses and serves startups, small and midsize businesses, managed service providers, and security-focused teams. Its product is designed to make shared authentication available from a browser rather than tying access to one employee’s phone. But one authentication method presented a different challenge: 2FA codes delivered through SMS . Many online services still send one-time passwords to mobile phone numbers. For teams managing shared accounts, those messages traditionally arrive on a physical phone controlled by one person. Daito needed a way to bring those SMS codes into the same controlled, collaborative experience as the rest of its 2FA platform. Spenza provided the programmable telecom infrastructure required to make that possible. The Result Daito enables customers to use a real mobile phone number while displaying incoming SMS verification and authentication codes directly inside a shared inbox . This eliminates the need for customers to purchase, provision, or manage a dedicated mobile phone, simplifying account verification workflows while preserving access to carrier-issued messaging. Daito now publicly offers this capability as its shared SMS inbox. Customers receive a real, non-VoIP mobile number, and incoming authentication codes become accessible inside Daito. The feature is currently commercialized as a paid add-on priced at $49 per number per month. Customer Overview Company Daito Product Web-based 2FA authenticator for businesses Primary Users MSPs, IT teams, agencies, technology companies, and security-focused businesses Core Use Case Securely managing and sharing 2FA access across teams Public Traction Trusted by 250+ businesses New Capability Shared inbox for SMS-based authentication codes Connectivity Partner Spenza Implementation Model Programmable mobile numbers, APIs, webhooks, and centralized line management The Challenge: SMS Authentication Was Still Tied to a Phone Daito had already created a secure way for teams to manage and share authenticator-based 2FA tokens. SMS authentication, however, remained dependent on traditional telecom infrastructure. When an enterprise account sent a code through SMS, the message normally arrived on a phone or SIM controlled by one employee. Other authorized users then had to wait for that person or ask them to forward the code. For MSPs and enterprise IT teams, this created several problems. Physical phone dependency Organizations often maintained dedicated phones or SIM devices solely for receiving authentication messages. This introduced: Hardware purchasing and replacement costs Charging, storage and device management Dependence on whoever had access to the phone Manual forwarding of sensitive messages Additional operational and security risks No application-level access to messages Consumer mobile subscriptions are designed for people using handsets. They do not normally provide a straightforward way for a software platform to receive incoming messages through an API. Daito needed incoming SMS messages to appear directly inside its application, not on a separate device. Scaling across enterprise customers A single MSP or enterprise could require multiple dedicated numbers for different customers, platforms or shared accounts. The target architecture needed to support: Multiple numbers per organization Rapid number provisioning Centralized activation and lifecycle management Reliable delivery of time-sensitive messages Separation between enterprise tenants Growth from hundreds to potentially thousands of managed lines These requirements formed the basis of the implementation delivered through Spenza. Why the Common Workarounds Were Not Enough Approach Limitation Dedicated mobile phones Adds hardware, maintenance, and dependence on physical access. Manual forwarding Slows down authentication and exposes codes through uncontrolled channels. Consumer mobile plans Provide no native provisioning, webhook, or tenant-management workflow. VoIP numbers May not be accepted by services that restrict virtual numbers. Separate carrier portals Force teams to manage connectivity outside the Daito experience. One shared number for everything Makes access control, customer separation, and auditing difficult. Daito needed more than a virtual-number provider. It needed a programmable mobile operating layer that could be embedded into its existing product. The Solution: Programmable Mobile Numbers Embedded into Daito Spenza delivered the carrier connectivity, provisioning workflows, APIs, billing controls and operational infrastructure behind Daito’s shared SMS inbox. Spenza’s wider platform combines carrier integrations, SIM and eSIM provisioning, billing, subscriber management, branded experiences, REST APIs and webhooks. This allows businesses to embed connectivity into an existing product without building and operating a full telecom stack internally. 1. Real, Carrier-Backed Mobile Numbers Daito can provide customers with real mobile numbers rather than relying solely on virtual VoIP numbers. Each number behaves like a standard mobile line and can receive SMS authentication messages from supported external services. The provisioning layer was designed to support: On-demand number allocation SIM or eSIM activation Number porting where supported Subscription activation and disconnection Assignment of numbers to specific customer accounts Expansion across additional operators and markets Callout: Real mobile identity The number presented to the external service is a carrier-backed mobile number. For the customer, the experience remains software-based and no end-user phone is required. Daito publicly states that its shared inbox uses real, non-VoIP phone numbers and has tested the service with commonly used platforms such as Microsoft, Google, Amazon and Facebook. 2. Incoming SMS Delivered into Daito When an SMS is sent to a provisioned number, the incoming message is processed through the connectivity and messaging layer and delivered to Daito’s application. The implemented workflow is: The customer does not have to check another device, access a carrier portal or ask a colleague to forward the message. 3. API and Webhook Integration Spenza APIs provided the developer layer required to integrate telecom functionality directly into Daito. The scoped API capabilities included: Purchasing or allocating a SIM or eSIM Activating a recurring mobile subscription Sending an outbound SMS where required Registering a callback for incoming messages Receiving SMS data through a callback API Retrieving message or subscription information Managing activation and line lifecycle events This architecture allows connectivity to behave like another software service inside Daito. Callout: Connectivity became part of the product Daito’s users interact with a shared SMS inbox. Spenza handles the telecom operations, carrier integration and mobile-line lifecycle behind that experience. 4. Tenant-Based Number Management Daito serves teams that may manage authentication across multiple customers, departments or business entities. The platform was therefore designed to map connectivity resources to Daito’s organizational structure. The solution supports: Dedicated numbers for different enterprise customers Number pools organized by tenant Provisioning tied to enterprise identifiers Separation of messages between organizations Role-based access inside the Daito application Usage and subscription reporting This tenant model helps prevent an authentication message intended for one customer from becoming visible to another. 5. Centralized Billing and Operations Alongside connectivity, Spenza provided the operating layer required to manage recurring telecom services. The implementation included: Centralized line and subscription management Prepaid credit management Automated low-balance notifications Usage and subscription reporting Billing for active lines Support for plan activation and ongoing charges Standard operational support This allowed Daito to introduce the feature as a commercial add-on without developing a separate telecom billing platform. The Results 1. A New Shared SMS Inbox Inside Daito Incoming SMS authentication codes can now be presented within the Daito experience, alongside the company’s existing shared 2FA workflows. Users no longer need to switch between Daito and a separately managed phone. 2. No End-User Phone Required Customers do not need to purchase, store, charge or circulate a dedicated mobile phone. Daito’s public service description confirms that authentication messages can be viewed inside Daito and that the customer does not need to purchase hardware. 3. Real Mobile Numbers Instead of a Basic VoIP Workaround The solution gives customers access to real, carrier-backed mobile numbers. This provides a stronger foundation for services that may treat mobile and VoIP numbers differently during verification. 4. A Commercial Add-On Daito Can Sell Daito has turned the capability into a customer-facing paid add-on. Its public offering currently lists each number at $49 per month , in addition to the customer’s Daito subscription. Business Impact Spenza delivered more than a telecommunications integration. It enabled Daito to launch a recurring connectivity-enabled product capability that complements its existing subscription offering. By embedding mobile services directly into the platform, Daito can increase customer value, strengthen recurring revenue opportunities, and differentiate its product without building telecom infrastructure from scratch. 5. Faster Provisioning and Centralized Management Instead of requesting lines manually through individual carriers, Daito can manage number allocation, activation and subscription workflows through an integrated platform and APIs. This reduces the operational effort required as more customers request SMS authentication numbers. 6. A Foundation for Enterprise Scale The solution was designed around Daito’s expected deployment pattern of multiple numbers per organization and hundreds of potential enterprise customers. The architecture supports: Automated provisioning Tenant-level resource management Centralized reporting Configurable message handling Additional operators and geographic markets Growth toward thousands of managed lines This creates a reusable infrastructure layer rather than a one-off integration. Before and After Spenza Before With Spenza Authentication codes tied to physical phones Codes available through Daito’s shared inbox Manual SMS forwarding Automated message delivery into the application Consumer mobile subscriptions Programmable line and subscription management Separate hardware and carrier workflows Connectivity embedded into Daito Difficult multi-customer management Tenant-based number organization Manual line activation API-driven provisioning Telecom cost handled separately Integrated billing and operational controls Limited path to scale Architecture built for large numbers of managed lines Why This Partnership Matters Most telecom services are still delivered as standalone products. Customers receive a SIM, a plan and access to a carrier portal. Daito and Spenza took a different approach. The mobile number is not the final product. It is a component inside a broader authentication workflow. The customer experiences: A shared SMS inbox Controlled access for team members Centralized authentication management No end-user phone requirement One software interface Behind that experience, Spenza manages: Mobile connectivity Number and line provisioning Carrier relationships Messaging delivery Subscription lifecycle Billing and reporting This is an example of telecom becoming embedded software infrastructure . Rather than asking Daito to become a telecom operator, Spenza provided the programmable connectivity layer required to extend Daito’s core product. About Spenza Spenza is an MVNO-in-a-box and connectivity management platform that helps businesses launch, embed and operate mobile services. Its platform brings together carrier integrations, SIM and eSIM provisioning, billing, subscriber management, branded portals, REST APIs, webhooks and connectivity plans across more than 180 countries. Spenza enables businesses to add connectivity to an existing product without building their own carrier integrations or telecom operating stack. Conclusion Daito’s journey shows how embedded connectivity can transform a traditional telecom dependency into a seamless software experience. By combining Daito’s expertise in shared authentication management with Spenza’s programmable mobile infrastructure, businesses can now access SMS-based 2FA codes through a secure, centralized workflow without relying on physical phones or manual forwarding. Spenza provided the foundation required to make this possible, from real mobile number provisioning and SMS delivery APIs to automated lifecycle management, billing, and scalable connectivity operations. Instead of building complex telecom infrastructure, Daito was able to focus on its core mission of helping teams securely manage authentication across organizations. The result is a new category of authentication workflow where mobile connectivity becomes an integrated product capability rather than a standalone service. With a scalable connectivity layer behind the scenes, Daito can continue supporting more customers, expanding enterprise use cases, and delivering a simpler, more secure way for teams to manage shared access. If your business wants to embed mobile connectivity, launch telecom-powered features, or add programmable SMS and voice capabilities without building carrier infrastructure from scratch, Spenza provides the APIs, platform, and operational foundation to help you launch faster and scale confidently. What Is IoT Connectivity Management? It enables organizations to manage mobile plans, device lifecycles, carrier relationships, and usage efficiently while reducing operational complexity.
